title: Add --platform host|<triple> override for dependency-edge evaluation
description:
Planning decision (2026-08-28, `/plan --deliberate`): cargo-depgate evaluates dependency edges for ALL platforms by default — no `--filter-platform`, every `resolve.nodes[].deps[].dep_kinds[].target` edge from the single `cargo metadata` run is kept — so policy results never depend on the runner OS (fail-closed). This follow-up adds an opt-in override for `cargo tree` parity: evaluate each edge's `target` cfg expression against the host triple or an explicit list of triples.

## Design

- Config: `[graph] platform = "all" | "host" | ["x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu", ...]` in `depgate.toml`.
- CLI: `--platform <all|host|triple>` (repeatable); CLI wins over config.
- Keep the single `cargo metadata` run (no `--filter-platform`) so one run serves any platform set.
- Evaluate `dep_kinds[].target` with `cfg-expr` (`targets` feature, builtin target DB — no `rustc --print cfg` subprocess) at edge-filter time; an edge survives if any selected platform activates it; `target = null` edges always survive.
- Host triple: `rustc -vV` host, with compile-time `TARGET` as fallback.
- Must not change the default (`all`).

## Context

Raised by the user during planning question Q3 (platform semantics), 2026-08-28. Sibling follow-ups to file on plan approval: `init` snapshot subcommand, SARIF output, metadata-json cache.
acceptance_criteria: 1) platform=host on Linux reproduces the edge set of 'cargo tree -p X -e normal' for the ganja-code fixture (differential test). 2) A cfg(windows)-only dependency is excluded under platform=host on Linux and included under platform=all and platform=[x86_64-pc-windows-msvc]. 3) Default (unset) behaviour is byte-identical to before the change. 4) An unknown triple is a config error (exit 2) with the offending depgate.toml line annotated.
